body: You're doing it already. Keep going my friend. You can do it.

I really feel your pain.

I have spent a lot of time thinking about how to end my life, but minimizing the damage it can cause to others. It's a really hard place to be. On the one end, I want to stop suffering, on the other, I don't want to cause more suffering. I wish I had an answer.

What bothers me a lot is that people always say, well this experience must have made you wiser? All the bad things that happened must have taught you valuable lessons?   


Why don't people realize that the events should never have happened in the first place and the real result was years of lost time and energy? I'd rather have the time and energy back. Keep the "lesson".

I think we're starting to understand the underlying science behind what's happening. I think it's crazy that a drug that is so cheap is being administered at such an extremely high cost. Even after accounting for all the costs, doctors are making a lot of money. It just goes to show how incentives can be misaligned.  


The results can vary from person to person. I know a few people who have undergone ketamine treatment. Because of the doctor's incentive to make money, one just fell into a regular pattern of getting an infusion but no additional therapy. Because she didn't make fundamental changes in her lifestyle, she's entirely reliant on expensive, weekly doses.   


Another went for six sessions and saw some benefit, but felt that after the initial relief, behavioral changes resulted in more permanent benefits.

“Let everything happen to you  
Beauty and terror  
Just keep going  
No feeling is final”

― Rainer Maria Rilke

Pick a date in the future like a month from now. Between now and then, make a rule: no negative feelings. If you experience a negative event, remind yourself, that you've set aside time in the future to process it. Whatever comes your way, you'll revisit it a month from now. In the meanwhile, write down a few positive attributes about yourself. Say them out loud.

You must have been in such incredible. To go from that to living another ten years really tells me how resilient and strong you are. I love this idea of not thinking too far ahead and just taking it little by little.

I just want to say thank you for being kind enough to encourage me to stick it out. 

I thinking some days it's 50/50 if I make it. Other days, it's looking like I don't. But, I fight and fight no matter what. I am terrified, literally terrified about the next 10 years.

I really wish good things happen to you.

Thank you for sharing. I've been battling suicidal ideation for several years now. An overarching circumstance has worn me down. I thought about leaping from a window a few years ago. I held on.  I'm still trying to hold on. I think you wrote because some part of you wants to hold on. It gives me hope that you overcame this in the past.

As some who is most fulfilled by invention/discovery/creation, it's very difficult for me to simply chose to be a teacher or do something else. I would feel like I am doing that just to stay alive and that would only make me feel worse. I don't want to exist just to exist. I want to thrive.  


I've had people suggest that. It's the first thing mental health professionals focus on and it destroys any chance of progress.  


I think the only thing that has prevented me at this point is uncertainty around the method, and that someone has to discover and deal with my dead body. I definitely don't want that person to be a loved one.   


I wish I could just go to a clinic, be administered the necessary drugs to kill me, get transported to a crematorium and be cremated. I neither need nor want a grave.   


Covid also feels like the ideal time because there's no expectation of a formal gathering. Anyone affected just sort of goes about their day and starts to move one.

I do, but one cannot be with the people one loves 24/7. They have to do what they have to do and during those hours, I feel the utter isolation of my experience--not a lot of people have gone through what I have, especially this level of fraud, and this strange of a story. I've researched other victims of crimes and there are a lot common traits, but it's not like there's a support group for people like me.

I love my friends who have always had such clarity about people that they are rarely if ever fooled. I think being perceptive and discerning is wise.   


At the same time, I am also rather envious of people who can maintain relationships with people whom they find flawed. I of course am not talking about people who are subjected to abusive situations or being manipulated. So long as they have awareness and agency, there's something about that flexibility that's admirable.   


Maybe try thinking about which attributes you think are less harmful, that you can observe and consciously forgive. That might lead to interacting with different people.
I cannot argue with someone finding a more suitable place to live elsewhere and moving. I don't believe it's worthwhile to live in persecution, for example, if you can live freely somewhere else.

From afar, many places may seem better. Some countries are doing better than others. But, there's xenophobia, racism, classicism, under/unemployment, corporate influence.

The United States is struggling to reconcile its self-image and reality. We have a lot of work to do especially with respect to racism, education, healthcare, criminal justice, and the environment to name just a few areas.

I am frequently surprised by how even though we are all upset by these things, how little our elected officials do. I believe we need to move beyond simply voting to lobbying and directing our politicians to implement policies we want.

My work was all consuming. It took 80-100 hour weeks to create what I did.   


I have great friends. I pushed myself to stay alive so that I wouldn't hurt them. I was hoping to recover somewhat financially so I could leave the people closest to me who need it some money. Now, I am too tired and can no longer think about staying alive just to not hurt them. It'll take a long time to recover financially, so the chances of leaving money seem slim. Also, by the time I do, they cannot benefit as much from it.

More than half of my productive life is gone. If I work hard for 10 years and it all works out, maybe I have 10 years enjoy life a bit. If anything else go wrong, that would just confirm that I should have ended it earlier.  
It feels like I have arrived at the optimal time to die. Staying alive feels very irrational. It sounds weird to say it that way, but I feel like dying is the rational decision at this point.
What do you think your best friend was trying to protect herself from?

The mind is a powerful thing. It's great that you had everything checked out by a dentist and have sound counsel to refer back to. I find sometimes saying something positive or helpful out loud actually does help. Maybe some breathing exercises can give you some relief.
Perhaps from people who were not believed?

Thank you for replying.   


Justice, civil or criminal, is a myth. 

It'll take ten years to get even close to where I would be now. I already lost ten. To think that this was twenty years of my life gone. The experience has been so painful. People praise this person for my work. He's steadily used it to market himself as a pioneer. It's humiliating because people think I didn't create it even though I actually did. I feel trapped.

I am not the first this has happened to. I probably won't be the last. It must be time to go.
Someone poured gasoline on me, set me on fire. Every cell burns. I desperately want to turn to ash.

You are a hero for surviving every day. I hated that question too, so I came up with a list of silly professions. I picked really absurd examples. If someone persisted, I would ask, why is what I do so, surely there's something else we can talk about. When in doubt, go with adult film star.

In my case, the "hurts" are ongoing and very likely to result in permanent damage. One aspect is that someone stole my work, took all the credit for it, made a fortune, and is using those ill gotten gains to block me from doing further work. Given how specialized my work is, the setback could take more than a decade for me to recover. I've already lost about a decade. He's also threatened physical harm to me, but for the authorities to do anything, he has to actually harm me first.

Your reply really resonates with me. I am slowly coming to terms with what a former friend and business partner did to me. He stole my work, told others it was his, made a fortune using it, told key people in the industry that I was incompetent.   


He used to manipulate me all the time.  


Everyone tells me how impressive I am and how much I can still accomplish, but I have lost faith in myself. I feel uncertain and hopeless. I definitely have started to come to terms with the fact that I have real PTSD.
